title: Catalase Activity Assay Protocol
author: Peter Havel
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.ygbftsn

steps.title: Prepare Formaldehyde Standard Wells
steps.instruction: Add the following components to the designated standard wells (tubes A-G) on the plate: 100 µl of diluted Assay Buffer, 30 µl of methanol, and 20 µl of standard per well.

steps.title: Prepare Positive Control Wells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of diluted Assay Buffer, 30 µl of methanol, and 20 µl of diluted Catalase (Control) to two wells.

steps.title: Prepare Sample Wells
steps.instruction: Add 100 µl of diluted Assay Buffer, 30 µl of methanol, and 20 µl of sample to two wells.

substeps.instruction: Ensure the amount of CAT added results in an activity between 2-35 nmol/min/ml.
If necessary, dilute samples with diluted Sample Buffer or concentrate using an Amicon centrifuge concentrator (100,000 MWCO) to reach the required activity level.

steps.title: Initiate Reactions
steps.instruction: Add 20 µl of diluted Hydrogen Peroxide to all wells as quickly as possible, noting the precise initiation time.

steps.title: First Incubation
steps.instruction: Cover the plate and incubate on a shaker for 20 minutes at room temperature.

steps.title: Terminate Reaction and Add Chromagen
steps.instruction: Stop the reaction and add the chromagen to each well.

substeps.instruction: Add 30 µl of diluted Potassium Hydroxide to each well to terminate the reaction.
Add 30 µl of Catalase Purpald (Chromagen) (Item No. 707017) to each well.

steps.title: Second Incubation
steps.instruction: Cover the plate and incubate for 10 minutes at room temperature on the shaker.

steps.title: Add Potassium Periodate and Final Incubation
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl of Catalase Potassium Periodate (Item No. 707018) to each well, cover, and incubate for five minutes at room temperature on a shaker.

steps.title: Measure Absorbance
steps.instruction: Read the absorbance of the plate at 540 nm using a plate reader.

steps.title: Calculate Catalase Activity
steps.instruction: Process the absorbance data to determine CAT activity.

substeps.instruction: Calculate the average absorbances of each standard and sample.
Subtract the average absorbance of standard A from itself and all other standards and samples.
Plot the corrected absorbance of standards as a function of final formaldehyde concentration (µM) from Table 1 to create a standard curve.
Calculate the formaldehyde concentration of the samples using the linear regression equation from the standard curve.
Calculate CAT activity, where one unit is defined as the amount of enzyme causing the formation of 1.0 nmol of formaldehyde per minute at 25ºC.
